Testing affect regulation via computational modeling of real-time alcohol choices in daily life — Sensitivity Analyses: Boundary Separation (B)

2026-06-13

1 About This Report

This report presents the sensitivity analyses for Boundary Separation (B) (B). These analyses re-estimate the primary models, but replace the current affective state used as the focal predictor in the main analyses with two alternative classes of affective predictor:

  1. Expected change in the affective state following alcohol use — participants’ prospective ratings of how consuming alcohol would change their stress / negative affect / positive affect (stores stress_change_alc, na_change_alc, pa_change_alc).
  2. Perceived change in the affective state vs. the last EMA assessment — participants’ reported change in stress / negative affect / positive affect relative to their previous assessment (stores perceived_stress_change, perceived_na_change, perceived_pa_change).

This gives six focal predictors in total. The modeling pipeline is otherwise identical to the primary analyses; the goal is to check whether the main conclusions hold under these alternative operationalizations of affective state. The focal predictor for each model is detected automatically from the fitted model formula.

For each focal predictor, the report is organized as follows:

  • Dimensionality reduction: PCA and UMAP component composition tables, showing which raw variables load most strongly onto each component.
  • GLMM results (raw features): Summary of results from GLMM model with raw variables.
  • Random forest results (raw features): Summary of results from random forest model with raw variables.
  • Model comparison: RMSE comparison table across all methods (GLMM, random forest, decision tree) and feature sets (raw, PCA, UMAP).
